sentence: Simvastatin is a statin, a medicine that lowers cholesterol by reducing how much the liver makes, and it is used to treat high cholesterol and to help prevent heart disease, including heart attacks and strokes.
note: NHS: used to lower cholesterol and prevent heart disease incl. heart attacks and strokes; stops the liver making cholesterol. MedlinePlus: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin), reduces risk of heart attack and stroke, slows cholesterol production.

sentence: Serious side effects are uncommon, but the NHS advises seeking help from a doctor for unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, and a GP or NHS 111 is the route for prompt advice.
note: NHS side-effects page: serious effects uncommon; seek help for unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness. 'GP or NHS 111' is site signposting wording, not quoted from the page.

sentence: Simvastatin is a type of medicine called a statin.
The NHS says it is used to lower cholesterol in people who have been diagnosed with high blood cholesterol.
It is also used to help prevent heart disease, including heart attacks and strokes.
A doctor may prescribe it when there is a family history of heart disease or a long-term condition such as rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes or type 2 diabetes.
Most adults can take simvastatin, and the NHS says it is sometimes prescribed to children aged 10 and over.
It comes as tablets and as a liquid that is swallowed, and it is also available in combination tablets with other cholesterol-lowering medicines.
In the UK, many simvastatin products are sold under the generic name, and the brand name Zocor also appears in the electronic Medicines Compendium.
note: emc ingredient listing: Zocor by Organon; most other products generic.

sentence: The NHS describes treatment as usually long term.
Simvastatin stops the liver from making cholesterol, which lowers the level of cholesterol in the blood.
It belongs to the group of medicines also known as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors.
Lowering cholesterol is one way of reducing the risk of heart attacks and strokes in people at high risk.
note: MedlinePlus: used to reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in high-risk patients, and to decrease cholesterol.

sentence: The NHS says it takes some weeks for cholesterol levels to fall.
note: Search summary: about four weeks; figure not repeated.

sentence: Because simvastatin works on cholesterol levels rather than on symptoms, a person may feel no different while taking it.
note: Textbook inference: high cholesterol itself usually causes no symptoms; not stated verbatim in retrieved text.

sentence: The NHS lists headache, dizziness, feeling sick, digestive problems, muscle aches and sleep problems as common side effects.
It says serious side effects are uncommon, affecting fewer than 1 in 1,000 people.
note: Search summary of NHS page: less than 1 in 1,000 may have a serious side effect.

sentence: Muscle problems are the ones to watch for.
note: NHS leaflet summary: muscle problems are the one to watch for.

sentence: The NHS advises seeking help from a doctor for unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness or cramps, which can signal muscle breakdown and kidney damage and can appear weeks or months after starting.
A GP or NHS 111 is the route for prompt advice.
note: Site signposting wording, not quoted from the page.

sentence: Yellowing of the skin or eyes, or pale stools with dark urine, can point to liver problems, and the NHS notes yellowing is harder to see on brown or black skin.
Severe stomach pain, which can be a sign of pancreatitis, and a pink-red rash are also listed as serious effects.
For breathing or swallowing problems, or a swollen face or throat, the NHS says to call 999 or go to A&E.
The NHS says grapefruit juice increases the level of simvastatin in the blood and makes side effects more likely, so it advises avoiding it.
Some medicines also raise the risk of serious side effects such as muscle damage.
The NHS lists the antibiotics clarithromycin, rifampicin and fusidic acid, the antifungals fluconazole and ketoconazole, some HIV medicines, hepatitis C treatments, warfarin, ciclosporin and danazol.
NHS Specialist Pharmacy Service guidance lists clarithromycin as contraindicated with simvastatin.
Where such a medicine is needed, the doctor may lower the simvastatin dose, switch to a different statin or pause simvastatin for a while.
The product information also limits the simvastatin dose with some heart medicines, such as amlodipine.
The NHS says drinking a lot of alcohol may increase the chance of muscle and liver side effects.
It says there is not enough information about herbal remedies and supplements taken with simvastatin.
A pharmacist or doctor can check any new medicine against simvastatin.

sentence: The NHS says simvastatin may not be suitable for people with liver or kidney problems, lung disease or an underactive thyroid.
A past muscle disorder, a history of myasthenia gravis and regularly drinking large amounts of alcohol are other reasons to check with a doctor first.
People are also asked to tell the doctor about unexplained ongoing muscle pain or a family history of muscle problems.
The NHS says simvastatin is not recommended in pregnancy because it can affect how the baby develops, and it gives separate advice for people planning a pregnancy.
It is not usually used in breastfeeding because it is not known whether it passes into breast milk, and a doctor may suggest a different statin.
During the first 12 months of treatment, a couple of routine tests are offered to check that the liver is working properly.

It therefore advises avoiding grapefruit juice with simvastatin.
